Shape unchanged for -63..61. The page gives no area, so no infobox comparison is possible.

The Lazica page: 'Between 69 and 79, a Laz admiral named Anicetus led his people in revolt against the Romans' and the kingdom is 'vassal of Roman Empire: 2nd to 5th century' in the infobox; the vassal tint is the roman-empire dossier's. The page says 'From the 2nd century onward, the Kingdom of Lazica grew increasingly powerful' and 'Although it did not extend its direct administrative control as far as Trabzon in the 4th century', but dates no expansion in 306; the step is kept at confidence 1 in the ledger. The page gives no area, so no infobox comparison is possible.

396 only: 17,022 km2, a one-year dip of 7,500 km2 with the Huns (Cliopatria) as neighbours 396-406. 'The division of the Roman Empire in 395 enabled Lazica to strengthen and expand', so no page supports a shrinking; treated as a Cliopatria artefact.
397-401: 23,475 km2, 1,050 km2 below the 395 outline; no page event (see 396). The 402 outline resumes.

402-533: 24,529 km2, back to the 306 outline. Dated within: Gubazes I's bid for independence in the mid-5th century, the Svans and Sanigs leaving Lazic control 'in the 470s', Tzath I installed by the Byzantine emperor in 523, the Persian occupation of Shorapani and Skanda in 528 and the Eternal Peace of 532 (Iberian War page) - none changes the Cliopatria outline. The page gives no area, so no infobox comparison is possible.

534-539: 24,650 km2 (+120 km2, noise); the Byzantine protectorate of 536 ('the Byzantine presence turned into a full protectorate', Lazic War page) is not a change of land. The page gives no area, so no infobox comparison is possible.

540-545: same outline; Cliopatria's row ends in 545, the year of the first truce, although the Lazic War runs to 562 ('The war in Lazica ended with the peace treaty of 562'). The kingdom does not end: Gubazes II rules to 555 and Tzath II follows in 556 ('The last king of Lazica'). The page gives no area, so no infobox comparison is possible.

562: the Fifty-Year Peace ends the Lazic War. 'By the Fifty Years Peace of Dara of 562, the Byzantine Empire was obliged to pay tribute to Persia each year' in return for Persia recognising Lazica 'as a Roman vassal state'; footnotes date the signing 561, the main text 562.

notes:
ONE STATE, TWO ROWS, ONE SPLIT ROW. (1) Cliopatria's Lazica (-63..545) and Kingdom of Lazica (638..777) share Wikidata Q136884 and the Wikipedia article: one kingdom. This dossier takes the earlier slug, lists Names ["Lazica", "Georgia"] and runs -63..637; kingdom-of-lazica (eu-19-c, already written, 638..777) is left alone, so the two are a hand-over (dissolve 637 here, found 638 there), not a merge. The orchestrator may merge them and keep one colour. (2) Cliopatria's Georgia row (567..2024) is not one state: 567-576 is Lazica (same outline as Lazica 534-545, 24,650 km2), 638-646 is Iberia/Kartli (reviewed in the georgia dossier, verdict wrong), 724-1009 is the Kingdom of Abkhazia (kingdom-of-abkhazia dossier, eu-19-x) and 1918-2024 is modern Georgia (georgia dossier). Only georgia_567 is reviewed here.

START AND END: Cliopatria's -63 is kept as the start although the page speaks of 'about the 1st century BC' and of 131 AD; 637 is a bookkeeping end. The page disestablishes the kingdom in 697 ('incorporated into the Byzantine Empire as a province' by the end of the 7th century; Sergius c. 696/697 acknowledges Arab suzerainty) and has the Kingdom of Abkhazia succeed it in the 770s (not on the Lazica page itself).

GAPS FILLED BY BRIDGING (confidence 1): 546-566 (the Lazic War, drawn as the 545 outline contested by Persia) and 577-637 (the 576 outline). The Persian hold on parts of Lazica (Petra to 551, Cotais and Uthimereos after 551, Souania/Svaneti) is dated only roughly on the Lazic War page, so the contest zone is the whole kingdom.

VASSAL TINTS: the eastern-roman-empire dossier has Lazica as its vassal 395-541, 551-617 and 626-632; the Lazica page puts 'vassal of Roman Empire: 2nd to 5th century' in the infobox, Sasanian influence in the early 6th century (Damnazes 'vassal of the Sassanids' to 521/522) and Arab suzerainty from c. 696/697. Those are the suzerains' ledgers (counterpart lazica), not written here.

CLIOPATRIA OVERLAPS: Lazica and Caucasian Iberia share no cells; the Lazica -63 shape is larger than the later ones by the Pontus Polemoniacus strip (Roman from 62).

PAGES: no page opened gives Pompey's treatment of Colchis (Aristarchus, 63-47, appears only in the colchis dossier), the date of Petra's construction (535), Persian withdrawal dates or Tzath I's 521 baptism. The infobox-style area is absent on every page opened, so no area ratio was possible.
